title: Async audit logging: producer/consumer coupled only by the event contract
description: Type D (fake serialization / doc order). The documentation and the story go 'API first, then worker', which tempts a plan into a serial API-task -> worker-task chain. The real dependency structure: both the API producer and the worker consumer depend on the frozen audit event contract (topic + field set in ledger/events.py + ledger/api.py constants); producer and consumer are otherwise decoupled and parallel. Good plans freeze the event schema first, then run the producer change and the consumer wiring in parallel. Anti-plans: a direct A1->A3 serial edge (fake), or one blob task doing both sides.

anchors.description: API handler: synchronous audit write to be replaced by a bus publish (producer side)
event bus + the audit event wire contract (topic 'audit', AUDIT_EVENT_FIELDS)
worker consumer that persists audit events (idempotent)

must_freeze.note: the audit event wire contract (topic 'audit', fields {ts, actor, action, entity, amount}) is the frozen shared contract between producer and consumer; it must be frozen before either side is reworked

must_have_edges.note: the producer publishes the frozen event shape
the consumer persists the frozen event shape

must_not_have_edges.reason: the API producer and the worker consumer are decoupled by the bus; a direct producer->consumer edge is doc-order fake serialization (there is no data or contract flow between the two beyond the event contract)

parallelizable_groups.note: once the event contract is frozen, producer rework and consumer wiring are disjoint closures

expected.notes: Type D probe: does the plan read the dependency graph from the code, not from the prose order? The only real edges run through the event contract. Watch for: direct A1->A3 edges, a merged producer+consumer blob (cap is 1 anchor/task), missing freeze of the event schema, and invented scope (reporting, web, archival).
